title: Constitution of Medina
summary: After Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Yathrib (Medina) in 622, a written agreement set terms between the Muslim emigrants, the Medinan Muslims and the Jewish groups of the town, making Muhammad arbiter of disputes. Its date is debated: most sources place it in the first year after the hijra, some after the Battle of Badr in 624.

uncertainty.note: Most sources in the WikiShia article place the pact in the first year after the hijra (fifth or eighth month); a minority place it after the Battle of Badr (2 AH / 624 CE). The Doha Institute abstract says composition is thought to have begun after the hijra.

where.historical_name: Yathrib, soon called Medina, in the Hejaz

importance.justification: Among the oldest documents of Islamic history; it frames the early Muslim community and its relations with other groups.

related.because: The text records arrangements made after Muhammad's migration to Medina.
